extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking publication with Catapult (authors of literary fiction and narrative nonfiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial mission and selection criteria for books Catapult publishes: literary fiction and artful narrative nonfiction that engage the publisher's 'Perception Box' metaphor and expand readers' ways of seeing. Focuses on voice, craft, diversity, and work that challenges assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes literary fiction and artful narrative nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catapult publishes literary fiction and artful narrative nonfiction that engages with the Perception Box; their books are positioned within these genres rather than commercial genre fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with the 'Perception Box'
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should engage with the Perception Box, the metaphor defining how we see others in their full humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should invite new ways of seeing and being seen — i.e., explore, challenge, or expand readers' perceptions of others and self.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provokes new ways of seeing
rubrics_metrics.description: Invites new ways of seeing and being seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books should prompt readers to reconsider assumptions and perspective; the publisher values work that changes or expands perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and vitality
rubrics_metrics.description: Written by vital voices—emerging and established—that honor the craft of writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catapult seeks voices with energy and distinctiveness who demonstrate respect for literary craft, whether they are new or well-known authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book qualities: alive, insightful, illuminating, surprising
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should be alive, insightful, illuminating, and surprising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations for tone and effect: prose that feels vital and provides new insights or revelations, including moments that surprise the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft and intention
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor the craft of writing and publish with care, intention, and respect for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catapult emphasizes careful editing and respectful author relationships; submissions should reflect considered craft and intentional choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges assumptions and biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace writers and audiences who fearlessly shake up our assumptions and biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred work questions dominant narratives and requires confronting or rethinking biases rather than comforting existing beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explores ambiguity and the 'space between the lines'
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrate stories that explore the space between the lines of our lives and raise questions rather than give answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narratives that prioritize nuance, ambiguity, and open-ended inquiry over didactic resolution are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disruptive impact: 'rattle the walls' of perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer work that rattles the walls of the Perception Box—expanding boundaries of who we think we are and what we know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catapult looks for books that have a disruptive or boundary-expanding cultural/intellectual effect on readers' understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to diverse and historically underrepresented voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with a diverse list of writers who have been historically underrepresented, broadening the literary landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions from or about underrepresented communities are prioritized as part of the publisher's mission to diversify literature in the U.S. and beyond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demanding, effortful reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace writing that requires effort from both writer and reader to reach beyond assumptions and biases to see humanity, struggle, and truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favored books may demand cognitive or emotional work from readers and should aim to reveal humanity and truth through that effort rather than easy consumption.
